page: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb-v2 is a bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal NVMe family. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 2388G processor featuring 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs with a dedicated allocation, operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The system configuration includes 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, which provides 8.0 GB of memory per core, and a local storage capacity of 3840 GB delivered via NVMe SSDs. The server does not include any GPU resources but comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2204.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 36.27 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 20287.03 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10222.0. While the Passmark memory score is positioned in the top tier at 3390.33, the system exhibits weaker performance in large-block uncached memory operations, with read and write bandwidths of 36.93 GB/sec and 19.38 GB/sec respectively.

Given its dedicated bare metal architecture and substantial local NVMe storage, this server offers high resource density and eliminates virtualization overhead, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for IOPS-demanding workloads. The hardware profile is well-suited for database hosting, static web serving at throughputs up to 12.59 GB/sec, and memory-intensive applications. It also supports lightweight machine learning tasks, achieving 275.61 tokens/sec for text generation on a small 135M parameter model.
